date.label: Undated Judges narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Samson's mother is instructed that no razor is to touch his head
claims.evidence: Judges 13:5 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The angel instructs Samson's mother that no razor is to touch the boy's head, because he will be consecrated to God from the womb. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Feldman et al. find transient European-related admixture in sampled early Iron Age Ashkelon individuals, amid predominantly Levantine ancestry; cannot establish Samson episodes.
claims.evidence: Feldman et al., Ancient DNA sheds light on the genetic origins of early Iron Age Philistines, Science Advances 5(7) (2019), read in full via PMC. The study examined ten individuals and found the early Iron Age population genetically distinct through a European-related admixture, a signal no longer detectable in the later Iron Age population; all three populations derive most of their ancestry from the local Levantine gene pool. Population-level evidence only; it names no biblical figure and cannot establish Samson episodes.

claims.claim: Timnah is conventionally linked to Tel Batash; not an archaeologically proven location for Samson's wedding.
claims.evidence: Biblical Archaeology Review, "Timnath" synthesis, read in full in Step 1. The site was discovered in 1871 by Charles Clermont-Ganneau and proposed as Timnah, which according to Joshua 15:10–11 lay between Beth Shemesh and Ekron; the identification is now accepted. In Iron Age I, Timnah was a fortified Philistine town, excavated from 1977 to 1989 by Amihai Mazar and George Kelm. The identification is a conventional scholarly association, not an archaeological proof of the episode: identifying a site and locating a named narrative event at it are separate evidentiary steps. (JCL-09-004's registry source_ids is S024, which has no registry entry and was not read — see review.notes; the claim is grounded by BARTimnah.)

claims.claim: Judges 15 narrates Samson's retaliation with three hundred foxes carrying firebrands that burn Philistine grain, vineyards and olives; his killing of a thousand Philistines with a fresh jawbone of an ass at Lehi, naming the place Ramath-lehi; and water given at En-hakkore after his prayer.
claims.evidence: Judges 15:1–20 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre; chapter 15 carries no Class A diff). Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1831), on Judges 15, read in full: on 15:4, "much controversy concerning the meaning of the term shualim, some supposing it to mean foxes or jackals," concluding he sees "no improbability in the common version"; on 15:17, Ramath-lehi, "The lifting up or casting away of the jaw-bone"; on 15:19, En-hakkore, "The well of the implorer." Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges, Judges 15, read in full: on 15:4, the word can mean jackals, which roam in packs, while keeping "foxes"; on 15:9, "The situation of Lehi is unknown"; on 15:15, the thousand "belong to the extraordinary character of the story"; on 15:17, Ramath-lehi as popular etymology, "casting away of the jawbone." This claim does not decide foxes vs. jackals; Lehi is unknown; the thousand is a narrative figure, not a verified casualty count. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Judges 16 narrates Samson carrying off the doors, posts and bar of Gaza's city gate; his betrayal by Delilah of the valley of Sorek for silver from the Philistine lords, his shaving, blinding and imprisonment at Gaza; and his death bringing down the house of Dagon at Gaza upon the Philistine lords and the crowd, after which he is buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.
claims.evidence: Judges 16:1–31 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). This claim deliberately does not quote 16:28. Context, not part of the proposition: no building in the Philistine cities has been securely identified as a temple of Dagon (BiblicalTraining Library, "Temples of Dagon," read in full: "So far, however, no building in the Philistine cities has been securely identified as his"); a Philistine temple excavated at Tell Qasile, in a phase dating to the 12th–11th centuries BC, had the roof of its main hall resting on two wooden pillars set on stone bases along the center of the room — that temple was not Dagon's, but it shows a Philistine sanctuary of the period could depend on a pair of central supports; Gaza lies beneath a modern city and only limited soundings were possible there in the 1920s. These context points neither prove the Gaza event nor identify its building. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

The [^S026] footnote stays in the MD, renamed to the registry ID, and resolves via the registry. S024 does NOT enter sources[]: it has NO registry entry (verified: no S024/Clifton/Timnah hits in the 296-entry registry) and was not read (Step 5 D-J09-2 R2 caveat: "Do NOT add S024 without reading it first"). JCL-09-004 is grounded by BARTimnah (BAR Timnath synthesis, read in full in Step 1, cited inline), not S024. JCL-09-002 is EXCLUDED from this category (J02/JCL-02-003 and J08/JCL-08-004 precedent): its registry final_editorial_instruction is "EXCLUDE from published factual claims; retain audit ID and rationale" — Numbers 6 and Judges 13 do not describe exactly identical Nazirite obligations. The prose discussion of the Judg 13 vs Num 6 comparison stays as-is (it presents resemblance + difference, not the excluded identical-obligations claim), and JADD-008 (the thematic connection) covers the relationship. Renumbering: the remaining claims are numbered sequentially (JCL-09-001->001, JCL-09-003->002, JCL-09-004->003, JCL-09-005->004, JCL-09-006->005; the excluded claim omitted). JCL-09-005 and JCL-09-006 are Step 4a new claims (new-claims-part1.md) and are NOT in the registry CSV. The draft's 16:28 Class A guard note is STALE and is NOT carried forward (J05 6:22 precedent): Phase 3 landed 2026-11-23 and the stored KJV Judg 16:28 now reads "O Lord GOD,"; the article does not quote 16:28, and JCL-09-006 deliberately does not quote it. JADD-008 is the 40th connection (SR-BUILD-1, D6): Judg 13:4–5 <-> Numbers 6:1–21, type thematic (NOT background), confidence probable. D6 (Yonatan, 2026-11-21) accepts JADD-008 as a qualified thematic connection on Nazirite restrictions; the note carries the D6 wording exactly and implies no identical requirements. No internal research IDs (JCL-/JADD-) appear in the reader-facing prose (the draft already contained none), and the prose is kept precise to what the claims state (Timnah is orientation, not a confirmed wedding site; the fox/jackal question is undecided; the thousand is a narrative figure; the building is called "the house," not a temple; the Numbers 6 comparison is fenced). The Timnah process-facing sentence was reworded to "The paragraph stays inside that narrowed wording." The AW-05 Dagon temple negative paragraph (under JCL-09-006) is preserved verbatim. primaryScripture is narrowed to Judges 13:1–25 (validator rule: a category's representative passage must span at most 3 chapters; fullRange stays Judg 13:1–16:31). Judg 13 is the representative passage — the birth/consecration announcement that defines Samson and anchors JCL-09-001 (Judg 13:5) and JADD-008 (Judg 13:4–5 <-> Num 6). Precedent in published categories: abraham-and-sarah (fullRange 12–25, primary 12–12), joseph-and-israel-in-egypt (fullRange 37–50, primary 46–46).
